page.framework: Google Accounts server-rendered Lite / client-enhanced Glif variants
page.notes: The generic evidence primitives received a lightweight server-rendered sign-in variant; Lighthouse received the fuller Glif variant. The audit covers the identifier entry, mobile reflow, raw no-JS view, and signup first step. Credentialed/password, account-management, recovery completion, and authenticated states are excluded.

findings.summary: The sign-in surface ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot is pixel-equivalent in appearance to the light capture, while the DOM reports color-scheme: normal and a white body background. The separate signup route does render dark, showing inconsistent preference support across the account journey.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply the same root-level light/dark color tokens used by the signup flow to sign-in; declare <meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark"> and color-scheme: light dark on :root.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly distinguished on the sign-in controls.
findings.evidence: The active focus probe found :focus-visible=true on the email input, links, and Next button, but every control computed outline-style:none and box-shadow:none. The focused-link screenshot shows no visible change, and the Lite sign-in DOM has no main landmark.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible outline or equivalent ring to every interactive control and place the primary sign-in content in a <main> landmark.

findings.summary: The full sign-in implementation misses the good LCP threshold under Lighthouse throttling.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 4.3 s and TTI at 6.1 s (performance 0.81). A separate unthrottled trace of the Lite response measured LCP at 0.843 s, so the regression is condition/variant-sensitive rather than universal.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the full Glif sign-in variant’s LCP dependency chain, prioritize its LCP text/font resources, and defer work that is not needed for the identifier step.

findings.summary: Redirect and font/script dependency chains delay the full sign-in render.
findings.evidence: The HAR shows three document redirects before the identifier page. Lighthouse reports a 686 ms longest network chain, including a 55 KB font, alongside the 4.3 s LCP.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse avoidable entry redirects and ensure only the critical font/style resources are prioritized for the identifier view.

findings.summary: The identifier step ships substantial code not used during initial render.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 361 KiB of removable JavaScript and 165 KiB of removable CSS; two JavaScript bundles are 64–73% unused in the measured view.
findings.suggestedFix: Split the account UI by step and load password, recovery, account-picker, and ancillary modules only when those states are reached; tree-shake unused CSS.

findings.summary: The authentication response has gaps in explicit browser-enforced policy.
findings.evidence: The headers probe found no Referrer-Policy header and a CSP policy containing unsafe-eval. Strong compensating controls are present, including HSTS, X-Frame-Options:DENY, nosniff, nonces, and require-trusted-types-for script.
findings.suggestedFix: Set an explicit restrictive Referrer-Policy and remove unsafe-eval from the remaining allow-list policy after a report-only compatibility rollout; preserve Trusted Types and nonce enforcement.

findings.summary: Unused client code adds avoidable transfer, parse, and memory cost to a simple identifier form.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 361 KiB unused JavaScript and 165 KiB unused CSS on a screen whose core UI is one text field and one primary button.
findings.suggestedFix: Use route/step-level code and style splitting so only identifier-step behavior is loaded before the user advances.

findings.summary: The public sign-in entry has no meta description.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe and Lighthouse both found a descriptive title but no meta[name=description].
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise description of the Google Account sign-in purpose while avoiding session-specific or sensitive content.
